text:
maria: Heads up — CI is flaking in eastus2 GPU pool, lots of short-lived 502s from microservices. Not sure if it's infra or app.
alertbot: [ALERT] kube-proxy high conntrack usage on node gpu-eu-eastus2-07 (90% nf_conntrack).
aj: Can you paste conntrack and sysctl dumps from one of the affected nodes?
maria: quick grab from gpu-eu-eastus2-07: 
```
$ sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
198750
$ sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144
$ dmesg | tail -n 5
nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
nf_conntrack: falling back to hashing
```
So it's basically full.
lee: That node is on the RDMA-enabled rack (SR-IOV). We're seeing lots of east-west ephemeral connections from model prefetchers + tracer processes. SR-IOV can change connection patterns (offload), but conntrack still counts when packets go through iptables hooks.
sam: Short term we can: increase nf_conntrack_max, tune conntrack hashsize, and lower nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established for this pool. Command to bump: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=800000` then persist in /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf.
aj: Also check ephemeral port exhaustion: `ss -s` shows high TIME_WAIT?
maria: `ss -s` shows high TCP: 
TCP: inuse 1420 orphan 0 tw 872 alloc 1576 mem 4
so TIME_WAIT numbers are high because clients open a lot of short flows.
ashley: Flushing conntrack with `conntrack -F` will restore services fast but will drop in-flight sessions. Not ideal for production but ok for quick mitigation if we coordinate drains.
oncall: How large will the blast radius be? Several tenant workloads on these nodes.
lee: Alternative immediate mitigation: pin heavy prefetch jobs to nodes without public egress (move them off nat-heavy rack), or route egress through a dedicated SNAT gateway so node-level conntrack isn't consumed by many ephemeral client->internal flows.
sam: Longer term: switch kube-proxy to IPVS (reduces conntrack pressure for service NATs), or adopt a BPF-based SNAT (Cilium e.g., with egress gateway) so we can centralize NAT. Also consider conntrack-per-node quotas via node-local conntrackd (experimental).
aj: For tonight: 1) bump nf_conntrack_max to 800k on affected nodes 2) set nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established lower to 1-2h 3) temporarily cordon & drain the top 2 nodes with highest counts and restart those pods 4) schedule a rolling restart of kube-proxy to pick up IPVS config test on a small canary.
maria: I'm going to run the bump on 4 nodes in the GPU pool and coordinate a conntrack flush on a drained node to minimize impact.
ashley: Make sure to update incident doc with exact nodes and times and tag customers if their SLAs are impacted :warning:.
aj: Also add a short-term monitoring alert for nf_conntrack usage per-node (threshold 70%) and add a dashboard for ephemeral port churn (TIME_WAIT growth rate).
oncall: Cost note — bumping conntrack and moving work around may add tail latency and some extra egress costs if we centralize NAT, but better than repeated 502s.
maria: OK doing the bump now, will post outputs.
(15m later)
maria: Done on nodes 07/08/09/10, conntrack counts dropped after draining and flushing one node at a time. Services recovered. Still seeing elevated counts during heavy prefetch windows.
lee: Follow-ups: 1) add node labels to isolate RDMA/SR-IOV hosts and schedule noisy prefetch jobs elsewhere 2) prototype kube-proxy IPVS on a canary pool 3) evaluate Cilium egress gateway for centralized NAT 4) test conntrackd evictions/softlimits.
aj: I'll open a short RFC for the IPVS + centralized SNAT plan and a runbook for conntrack floods.
maria: Thanks all — will keep monitoring and post a postmortem if things reoccur. :thumbsup:
